Symptoms.title: How are you feeling?
Symptoms.intro: Describe your symptoms in your own words, in English or Kinyarwanda. MamaCare checks them against WHO pregnancy danger signs and tells you how urgent they are and what to do next.
Symptoms.emergency: In an emergency, don't wait: call 912 or go to the nearest health facility.
Symptoms.placeholder: For example: "I have had a bad headache since this morning and my vision is blurry"

bleeding.label: Bleeding
bleeding.text: I am 24 weeks pregnant and started bleeding from my vagina this morning.

headache.label: Headache and blurred vision
headache.text: I have a very bad headache that won't go away and my vision is blurry.

nausea.label: Morning sickness
nausea.text: I feel a bit sick in the mornings and tired, but I have no pain.

levels.red: Urgent: go to a health facility now
levels.yellow: See a health worker within 24 hours
levels.green: Can usually be managed at home

Danger.title: Danger signs: go now
Danger.intro: If you have any of these, go to the nearest health facility immediately. Do not wait for your next appointment.
pregnancy: Severe headache, blurred vision or seeing spots
Water leaking or breaking before labour
Baby moving less than usual, or not moving
Swelling of the face and hands
Vomiting so much you cannot keep fluids down
Danger.getHelpIntro: See a health worker the same day if you notice any of these. For a newborn, do not wait.
baby: Not feeding, or too sleepy to wake for feeds
Fewer wet nappies than expected, or dark urine
Yellow skin or eyes, especially in the first day or on the palms and soles
Fast breathing, vomiting everything, or fits
breastfeedingMother: Fever with a red, hot, painful area on the breast
Pus or blood from the nipple
Pain that does not improve after fixing the latch
Feeling very low, anxious, or unable to cope
postpartum: Fever, severe headache, chest pain, or breathing difficulty
Persistent sadness, hopelessness, or harmful thoughts
